notices.Title: Langley Wood National Nature Reserve - tree felling contract
notices.Title Compact: Langley Wood National Nature Reserve - tree felling contract
notices.Description:
Background to the job:
Natural England is managing ash dieback and hazardous trees along roads and footpaths. It is important that work is carried out sensitively and as specified, ensuring unnecessary damage to the woodland is avoided.
Timing:
Work must be completed by 28th February 2027, to avoid disturbance to nesting birds.
Nature of the job:
•	Climbing ash trees is not permitted.
•	The supplier will have the responsibility for carrying out checks of PRFs (Potential Roost Features). The supplier must have a trained person on site who is qualified to inspect PRFs for bat roosts. Supporting documentation of relevant training to be submitted with quote.
•	With reference to the attached spreadsheet (Tree safety works 2026_27):
-	Trees with PRFs will require inspection by a qualified person immediately prior to felling. If the PRF is identified as an active roost, work must stop on that tree immediately. If no active roost is present, the tree can be felled.
-	Trees with no PRFs can be felled without further inspection.
•	Any trees with PRFs that cannot be checked due to access issues should not be felled. A record of these trees must be kept and submitted to your contacts at Natural England.
•	Trees to be felled have been sprayed clearly with the correlating number
•	Trees to be reduced or dead-wooded will have a small yellow dot sprayed at the base
•	Secondary identification tags are present in some cases.
•	No felling over the NNR boundary is permitted unless agreed in advance.
•	Trees must be felled to minimise damage to adjacent trees. The following is acceptable:
o	Coppicing hazel or felling birch to clear the direction of fell
o	Damage to oak branches below 10cm in diameter - providing no potential bat roosts are disturbed and no branches are left hanging from the canopy.
•	For trees being felled with approximate diameters of 15cm or more, the main bole should be left whole if not on a path or boundary. Everything else can go into brash piles. In no access areas, the crowns do not need to be broken down, unless it's obviously unsafe.
•	All other timber (below 15cm diameter) to be stacked in 2m lengths where convenient.
Site considerations:
Access by vehicle is only permitted as per the attached access map, vehicles must not be driven off the hard standing. Tracks are suitable for ATV/quad bikes only. 4 x 4 pick-ups/Land Rovers should only be used on the purple tracks (see site map). Any track or ground damage must be made good at the expense of the contractor..

notices.Title: Manchester Worklessness Programme
notices.Title Compact: Manchester Worklessness Programme
notices.Description:
Manchester City Council (MCC) wishes to commission a service which can meet the following key objectives: 
- Reduce the barriers to employment for Manchester residents 
- Engage and support people who are not in employment to participate in the labour market 
- Support people in work, at risk of falling out of work due to health conditions or disabilities, to remain in employment 
- Engage employers to provide meaningful work opportunities 
- Deliver a coherent, joined-up local work, health and skills offer 
The Manchester Worklessness Programme will be based on the following principles: 
- Delivering Making Manchester Fairer  
- Targeting support in the right places/neighbourhoods and aligning to Live Well  
- Intervening early to prevent unemployment and support those furthest away to move closer to work  
- Addressing known inequality of access to good employment for racially minoritised groups 
- Strengthening the city's approach to the social model for disability 
- Delivering Manchester City of Learning 
- Working closely with partnerships to develop an integrated local offer between the provider and grass roots organisations
The Worklessness Programme will deliver a Supported Employment and a wider early medium-intervention Employment Support Service, providing participants with holistic support for their barriers to employment, including health-related concerns. 
Delivery will follow a keyworker model, ensuring culturally competent, multidisciplinary support tailored to individual needs. Where required, the provider will work with external partners to deliver specialist interventions, including support for mental health, wellbeing, and English language development. 
The service will also act as a triage and referral hub, linking participants to the wider local work and health system. Where needs fall beyond the programme's scope, the keyworker will signpost or refer participants to appropriate local services and follow up to ensure support is received.
Further information is provided in the Specification.
Manchester City Council invites Applications for the provision of the Services, from organisations with relevant experience and ability to demonstrate sufficient capacity for providing the Services.
The Contract will be for an initial term of 26 months. The Council may extend for a further period of time of 12 months. 
It is intended for the contract to commence 01 February 2027. 
The Council currently has approved funding of approximately £1 million in respect of the initial requirements under this procurement. Therefore, the guaranteed minimum value of the contract is £1 million.
The Council may, subject to governance approvals and the availability of funding, seek to procure additional services of a similar nature during the contract term; it is planned for matched third-party funding from the Greater Manchester Integrated Settlement of c£3m to be potentially added to this tender by October 2026. Should such approvals be obtained for this additional funding, the total value of the contract may increase to an estimated maximum value of approximately £4 million. 
Bidders should note that the Council gives no guarantee that any expenditure above the currently approved funding level will be commissioned. Any additional requirements will be subject to separate internal approvals and budget availability. Tenderers should therefore not rely on the Council exercising any option to increase expenditure beyond the currently approved requirement. 
The Council will assess bidders on their ability to perform the contract as advertised, including the potential requirement to deliver services with an estimated maximum contract value of approximately £4 million. 
It is envisaged that the contract will be awarded to one (1) lead provider or consortium.

notices.Description:
Preliminary Market Engagement (PME)/soft market test related to the provision of Supported Accommodation for Young People aged 18 and over. 
Please note this is not an opportunity to tender but is an information gathering exercise to inform the Councils future requirement.
The proposed service will be for care leavers aged 18-21 (up to 25 in some cases) with low to moderate support needs and will provide:
• Safe, good-quality shared accommodation within Leicestershire
• Flexible, needs-led support that allows young people to progress into independent living
• Help to young people to build; Practical life skills; Emotional resilience; Social integration

The purpose of this PME is to gauge interest from the market and to investigate potential options for the service described above.

notices.Title: T/HR061/26 Tooling and Storage Tender for ESS (Sweden)
notices.Title Compact: T/HR061/26 Tooling and Storage Tender for ESS (Sweden)
notices.Description: The European Spallation Source (ESS) is a European Research Infrastructure Consortium (ERIC) committed to the goal of building and operating the world leading facility for research using neutrons. Once constructed in Lund, Sweden, it will provide new opportunities for researchers in a broad range of scientific areas including life sciences, energy, environmental technology, cultural heritage, and fundamental physics. It will be an accelerator-based facility producing neutrons for a large array of advanced instruments. The UK is a partner in construction of the ESS alongside 15 other European countries and has committed significant funding for construction. The Science and Technology Facility Council (STFC) is managing the UK contribution to ESS. The Active Cell Facility is one such contribution to be delivered by Remote Applications in Challenging Environments (RACE) — a department of the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) (the ‘Purchaser’). Inside the Active Cells exhausted, highly radioactive parts involved in the neutron generation will be size reduced using remote handling technologies and removed for confinement. UKAEA are undertaking delivery of the Tooling Storage System, comprising six storage devices designed to house remotely operated tooling within the Active Cells. The scope of this tender is to manufacture, assemble, test and deliver to Sweden the following items: Shaft Cutting Station (SCS) Support Plate Storage Device Proton Beam Window (PBW) Strongback and Deployable Camera Stand (DCS) Storage Device Modular Wall Storage (MWS) Device, including Bolting Tool Caddies Chain Storage Device Storage Containers Cable Spooling Tool Testing shall include mechanical static checks, functional testing, and structural testing in accordance with the FAT plan.

notices.Title: NHSE1108  L&D and RECONNECT Services, Enhanced RECONNECT Services and MH Treatment Requirement Services
notices.Title Compact: NHSE1108  L&D and RECONNECT Services, Enhanced RECONNECT Services and MH Treatment Requirement Services
notices.Description:
Liaison and Diversion and Reconnect Services, Enhanced Reconnect Services and Mental Health Treatment Requirement Services for Lancashire and Cumbria 
North of England Commissioning Support (NECS) is a commissioning support service working for and on behalf of NHS England - North West (the Relevant Authority) who are undertaking a market engagement process via RFI to commission Liaison and Diversion and Reconnect Services, Enhanced Reconnect Services and Mental Health Treatment Requirement Services for Lancashire and Cumbria under the NHS Standard Contract.
Liaison and Diversion (L&D) services aim to provide early intervention for vulnerable people as they come to the attention of the criminal justice system. L&D services provide a prompt response to concerns raised by the police, probation service, youth offending teams or court staff, and provide critical information to decision-makers in the justice system, in real time, when it comes to charging and sentencing these vulnerable people. RECONNECT services aim to improve the wellbeing of people leaving prison, reduce inequalities and address health-related drivers of offending behaviours.
Enhanced RECONNECT (ER) service builds upon the RECONNECT programme as an enhanced pathway of care. The ER service will work in  collaboration with partners, including those from across government to ensure that individuals that have been identified as high risk to the public and have complex health needs that may impact on their risk of reoffending
Primary Care Mental Health Treatment Requirement (MHTR) service  aims to support individuals whose offending behaviour is linked to mental health needs by providing timely assessment, treatment and therapeutic interventions within Primary Care. The service seeks to offer courts an effective alternative to custodial sentences, address the underlying factors contributing to offending, and reduce the likelihood of reoffending.
Proposed Contract Start Date: 01/10/2027
Closing date for submission of the RFI response is by 5pm 4th September 2026
